title: Human Dignity and Justice
subtitle: How Islamic ethics guides truthful, compassionate speech about Palestine
summary: Islam commands Muslims to protect human dignity, establish justice, and speak truthfully—even when discussing people or causes they strongly oppose.

sections.title: Justice Is an Islamic Obligation
sections.body: Islam does not make justice conditional on nationality, religion, or political sympathy. The Qur'an commands believers to stand firmly for justice and to tell the truth even when it is difficult. This gives Muslims a clear moral framework for speaking about Palestinian lives and every other human life.

sections.title: Justice Even When Emotions Run High
sections.body:
The Qur'an says:

"O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted." (Qur'an 4:135)

This command rules out selective justice. A Muslim may oppose oppression while still acknowledging facts that complicate his preferred narrative, condemning crimes committed by anyone, and refusing to assign guilt to an entire people.

sections.title: Do Not Let Hatred Cancel Justice
sections.body:
The Qur'an gives an even more direct command:

"O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do." (Qur'an 5:8)

The verse does not ask Muslims to ignore wrongdoing. It teaches them to name wrongdoing accurately, reject collective blame, and protect innocent people even when anger is understandable. Justice is part of worship because it is obedience to Allah.

sections.title: How to Speak and Act Responsibly
sections.body:
Distinguish civilians from governments, armed groups, and political parties. Check the date, location, author, and original evidence behind a claim before repeating it. Do not circulate unverified casualty figures or images, and do not treat another community's suffering as a debating tool.

A faithful response can include sincere prayer, lawful charity through accountable organizations, learning from reliable sources, and principled advocacy. It must not include dehumanization, false testimony, celebration of civilian deaths, or hatred of people because of their identity.

sections.title: Accountability Without Collective Blame
sections.body:
If an armed group attacks civilians, justice requires identifying the responsible actors and condemning the attack. It does not make every member of a surrounding population guilty. If a government uses unlawful force, the same principle applies: distinguish the government's policy, the actions of particular units, and the civilians who may be harmed or may oppose it.

This distinction strengthens accountability. It protects the innocent, makes moral judgment more precise, and prevents grief from being turned into hatred.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Human Dignity and Justice
sections.body: Islam offers a clear standard: honor human life, establish justice, verify claims, and refuse collective blame. The Qur'an requires Muslims to remain just even toward people they oppose. Applying that standard to Palestine means defending the oppressed, condemning attacks on civilians, and speaking truthfully about every side.

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًۭا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًۭا
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
